headline: Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium enrichment dispute, mediators warn of renewed conflict, says reports
body:
Published - November 21, 2026 04:08 pm IST - Tehran, Iran

Abbas Araghchi said Iran was seeking a “good, honourable and lasting agreement” rather than remaining in a situation of “neither war nor peace”. File photo | Photo Credit: AP

Negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled over disagreements concerning Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile, with mediators warning that they cannot guarantee a return to military escalation in West Asia.

Washington is insisting on a clear roadmap and written guarantees from Iran that it will eliminate its enriched uranium stockpile and refrain from resuming uranium enrichment in the future, Al Arabiya English reported, citing a senior source. However, both sides have maintained firm positions on the issue despite several proposals put forward by mediators to bridge their differences, the report said.

The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme. Earlier, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran would not accept an agreement with Washington merely to end the current diplomatic impasse, insisting that any settlement must protect Iran's national interests and provide assurances against another military confrontation.

headline: U.S. court dispatches summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun case
body:
Updated - November 21, 2026 08:35 pm IST - Washington

On November 13, the Southern District Court of New York ordered that summonses be issued to Doval and Goel, citing the Hague Convention. File | Photo Credit: PTI

A U.S. court has dispatched summonses to National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) Director Samant Goel to be served through Indian courts in connection with a case involving an alleged murder plot against Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.

Pannun, legal counsel for the banned organisation Sikhs for Justice (SFJ) who is wanted in India on several terror charges, has filed the civil lawsuit seeking damages over an alleged attempt on his life.

The clerk of the Southern District Court of New York said that the summonses were sent through courier company FedEx to the Patiala House Court, Tis Hazari Court, and the Dwarka District Court in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026).

The Southern District Court of New York had ordered earlier this month that summonses be issued to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel after noting that Pannun’s earlier attempts to personally serve notices on the two were blocked.

“The Court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,” read an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla.

headline: EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt
body:
Published - November 22, 2026 06:15 pm IST - Antalya

Darragh O'Brien, minister of climate, energy and the environment of Ireland, left, and Wopke Hoekstra, EU climate commissioner, speak outside a plenary session at the COP31 U.N. Climate Summit on November 22, 2026, in Antalya, Turkey. | Photo Credit: AP

The European Union on Sunday (November 22, 2026) rejected a climate deal that omits any mention of fossil fuels, as the UN climate talks in Türkiye pushed into record extra time.

Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said the EU and its member States “object” to the pact because it “does not meet the moment”.

“We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” Mr. O’Brien told a chaotic closing session a record 44 hours after the summit’s official end. Panama, a vocal critic of the COP process that had threatened to walk away from the talks, also formally objected to the proposed deal as the summit plunged into a tumultuous finale.

The proposed deal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations, but many States had expressed frustration that the draft did not refer to coal, oil or gas. “We will not accept negotiating backwards in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” said Mr. O’Brien.

headline: North Korea delays international marathon until October: tour agency
body:
Updated - November 22, 2026 12:37 pm IST - Seoul

A participant of the Pyongyang marathon runs down Mirae Scientist Street. File | Photo Credit: AP

North Korea has postponed its annual international marathon, which gives runners from around the world a rare glimpse of the secretive state's capital city, by six months until next October, a tour agency has said.

The race, which has historically seen hundreds of local and foreign athletes pound the streets of Pyongyang before finishing in front of thousands of fans at Kim Il Sung Stadium, is the diplomatically isolated state's largest international sporting event.

It was held last year for the first time since the Covid-19 pandemic, but this year's race, scheduled for April, was cancelled with no reason given.

The next edition, initially slated for April 2027, will now take place in October, Beijing-based Koryo Tours, which describes itself as the marathon's exclusive partner, said.

The company "has been informed by our partners in the Pyongyang International Marathon Committee that the date for the 2027 marathon is being changed", it said on its website on Saturday (November 22, 2026).

"It will not take place in April 2027. Instead, it is almost certain that the 2027 Pyongyang International Marathon will happen in October 2027," it added.

"We hope to have a fully confirmed date in good time," it said, without giving a reason for the change.

headline: European Union proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
body:
Updated - November 21, 2026 06:03 pm IST - Brussels (Belgium)

European Council President Antonio Costa. File | Photo Credit: AP

The European Union (EU) put forward plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to fund its next budget on Saturday (November 21, 2026), as it seeks to bridge divisions among member states over the bloc's long-term funding.

European Council president Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros ($224 billion) a plan initially put forward by the European Commission, which some countries had slammed as too onerous.

"I believe this proposal can bring us closer to a final agreement," Mr. Costa told a press conference in Brussels.

EU countries have been squabbling over the size of the next budget, with Germany leading calls for major cuts after the Commission last year proposed a two-trillion-euro budget for the 2028-2034 period.

Berlin criticised a revised proposal published last month that suggested slashing the bloc's future seven-year budget by 140 billion euros.

Mr. Costa, who represents the EU's 27 states, is seeking to reach a deal by the end of the year balancing contributions from member states with new sources of revenue for the bloc.

Among these could be a tax on digital firms that the draft Mr. Costa presented on Saturday says will concern companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU as well as a global turnover of more than 750 million euros.

headline: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones hit Russian warship at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
body:
Updated - November 23, 2026 11:07 am IST - Cairo

A combination of satellite images shows a Russian corvette and the northern port area before (above) and after an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base, with the latter image showing the vessel capsized, in Benghazi, Libya, November 21 and 22, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

A suspected Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship on Sunday (November 22, 2026) at a naval base in Libya, officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.

The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said.

They said that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, they said.

The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.

Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime dictator Muammar Gaddafi, who was later killed, in 2011. A UN-supported government is based in Tripoli, and a rival administration is located in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.
